record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; code and artifacts were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports mean-difference direction extraction and direction removal, with refusal and utility results on Gemma and its Lapa adaptation. It applies this method in a new bilingual/model-transfer setting.
record.gate_note: README-reported results only. The persona-steering section uses a different, persona-derived direction, so its outcomes are not rows for the refusal-direction claims. Selection settings and validation values are not outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study applies the original difference-in-means extraction and directional ablation (harmful vs harmless prompts, block selection, removal at all layers) to Gemma 3 and its Ukrainian adaptation Lapa. It reports refusal counts (Jev) and safety counts (Llama Guard 4) against a random-direction control. The new elements are cross-language (English-extracted direction on Ukrainian requests) and cross-model (Gemma direction removed from Lapa). This is a new setting with results on V1 and V6, so T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README claims the Gemma-extracted direction transfers to Lapa without target training, raising unsafe labels and cutting refusals in both languages, with near-unchanged Belebele accuracy. Two points should be added. The authors stress that Llama Guard safety and Jev refusal labels are not opposites. They also report that the separate persona-steering directions do not induce refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an English activation-mean difference from 128 harmful and 128 harmless prompts, selects a block using validation requests, then removes the direction at all 48 block inputs and attention/feedforward residual contributions. This is a bilingual Gemma-to-Lapa transfer experiment and repository, not stated to be an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports English and Ukrainian results separately and compares transferred Gemma directions with native Lapa and random directions. Direction selection uses a harmless next-token KL limit of 0.1 nats; Gemma selects block 32 and native Lapa block 34.

fits_no_version.finding: A persona direction (cautious-answer activations minus practical-answer activations) was added or subtracted at layer 32. It produced 0/20 coherent refusals on legitimate questions, matching the original model. Full-response random steering reduced coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response-persona-derived directions do not induce refusal when added to the residual stream.

record.problems: README-only evidence; code and artifacts were not read or run. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Capability evidence is limited to Belebele reading comprehension. Refusal labels remain after removal in every reported setting.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted. Persona-steering results are not included because they use a persona-derived direction rather than the refusal direction; the README reports no coherent refusals induced by those persona settings on 20 legitimate questions.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal is not reported for the refusal direction. Capability beyond Belebele reading comprehension is not tested. Results on the 100 benign JBB requests are not shown.
Languages other than English and Ukrainian, other model families, and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested.

missing.what: Outcomes on the 100 benign JBB requests per language (over-refusal or harmlessness after removal) are described in the method but not reported.
missing.locator: README, Method ('100 JBB benign requests per language')

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is README-only: there are no uncertainty estimates, the artifacts are access-gated, and the repository dates (2026) are unusual. Lapa refuses only 83/339 harmful requests at baseline, so absolute refusal reductions in Lapa are small. The Llama Guard rows measure output safety, not refusal, which is why their counts move much less than the Jev refusal counts.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports removal results, but not adding the refusal direction. Utility is checked only with Belebele reading comprehension, not a broad capability suite.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The README compares Gemma and native Lapa directions but does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
Safety and refusal judges are both reported, but no representation-level test of separate harmfulness and refusal encodings is described.
Transfer is tested from Gemma to Lapa and across English and Ukrainian; other model variants, base-to-instruct transfer, and other languages are not tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.

tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means extraction and all-layer ablation as Arditi et al., but the main result is a new setting: transfer to Ukrainian requests and to the Lapa adaptation. The judges also differ (Jev rubric, LG4). T1 would also be defensible for the Gemma English rows.

source_check.notes: The source is a README only, with no CIs, one random seed and n=339 harmful requests per language. The Jev judge model and the model sizes are not stated (48 blocks suggests about 12B, but the text doesn't say). Lapa's native direction is also English-extracted, so r20 is cross-language too. The README reports no direction-addition (refusal induction) test, and the persona-steering directions do not induce refusal (0/20).
